155:                 .party_authority()
156:                 .gateway_bucket()
157:                 .filter(0u8)

165:                         .minutes;
166:                     let party_id = party.id;
167:                     Some((
168:                         party_id,
169:                         EXACT_CASE_CONTEXT_CONTACT_REF.to_string(),
170:                         character_alive_at_for_view(ctx, row.character_id, minute),
171:                     ))
172:                 })
173:                 .collect(),
174:             CharacterContextKind::StrategicEncounter => ctx
175:                 .db
176:                 .party_authority()
177:                 .gateway_bucket()
178:                 .filter(0u8)
179:                 .filter_map(|party| {
180:                     ctx.db
181:                         .strategic_encounter()
182:                         .party_id()
183:                         .find(&party.id)
184:                         .filter(|encounter| {
185:                             encounter.encounter_id == row.context_id
186:                                 && encounter.status == StrategicEncounterStatus::AwaitingChoice
187:                         })
188:                         .map(|encounter| {
189:                             (encounter.party_id, row.context_id.clone(), character.alive)
190:                         })
191:                 })
192:                 .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
193:             CharacterContextKind::RoadEncounter => ctx
194:                 .db
195:                 .road_challenge_authority()
196:                 .gateway_bucket()
197:                 .filter(0u8)
198:                 .filter(|challenge| challenge.id == row.context_id && challenge.is_open())
199:                 .map(|challenge| (challenge.party_id, challenge.id, character.alive))
200:                 .collect(),
201:         };
202:         for (party_id, contact_ref, alive_at_frontier) in parties {
203:             let contact_id = party_context_contact_id(&party_id, &row.context_id);
204:             let revision = if matches!(
205:                 row.context_kind,
206:                 CharacterContextKind::CaseSite | CharacterContextKind::HostileGroup
207:             ) {
208:                 row.revision
209:             } else {
210:                 ctx.db
211:                     .party_context_contact_authority()
212:                     .id()
213:                     .find(&contact_id)
214:                     .map_or_else(
215:                         || {
216:                             if row.context_kind == CharacterContextKind::StrategicEncounter {
217:                                 ctx.db
218:                                     .strategic_encounter()
219:                                     .party_id()
220:                                     .find(&party_id)
221:                                     .map_or(row.revision, |encounter| encounter.revision)
222:                             } else {
223:                                 1
224:                             }
225:                         },
226:                         |contact| contact.revision,
227:                     )
228:             };
229:             let treatment_limb = adventuresim_core::physiology::BodyRegion::ALL
230:                 .into_iter()
231:                 .find(|limb| {
232:                     ctx.db
233:                         .limb_injury()
234:                         .character_id()
235:                         .filter(row.character_id)
236:                         .find(|injury| injury.limb == *limb)
237:                         .is_some_and(|injury| injury.cut_damage > 0.0 && !injury.bandaged)
238:                 });
239:             let incapacitated = ctx
240:                 .db
241:                 .character_strategic_condition()
242:                 .character_id()
243:                 .find(row.character_id)
244:                 .is_some_and(|condition| {
245:                     condition.status
246:                         == adventuresim_core::morale::IncapacitationStatus::Incapacitated
247:                 });
248:             let emergency_bandage = row.treatment_decision != ContextualDecisionState::Refused
249:                 && treatment_limb.is_some_and(|limb| {
250:                     ctx.db
251:                         .limb_injury()
252:                         .character_id()
253:                         .filter(row.character_id)
254:                         .find(|injury| injury.limb == limb)
255:                         .is_some_and(|injury| {
256:                             adventuresim_core::strategic_action::emergency_bandage_is_necessary(
257:                                 incapacitated,
258:                                 adventuresim_core::surgery::SurgeryProcedure::Bandage,
259:                                 injury.cut_damage,
260:                                 injury.bandaged,
261:                             )
262:                         })
263:                 });
264:             result.push(BackendContextCharacter {
265:                 party_id,
266:                 contact_ref,
267:                 context_kind: row.context_kind,
268:                 location_id: row.location_id.clone(),
269:                 character_id: row.character_id,
270:                 role: row.role,
271:                 ordinal: row.ordinal,
272:                 alive: alive_at_frontier,
273:                 revision,
274:                 membership_revision: row.revision,
275:                 contact_decision: row.contact_decision.presentation(),
276:                 treatment_decision: if row.treatment_decision
277:                     == ContextualDecisionState::Unavailable
278:                     && emergency_bandage
279:                 {
280:                     InteractionPresentationDecision::EmergencyTreatment
281:                 } else {
282:                     row.treatment_decision.presentation()
283:                 },
284:                 treatment_limb_slug: treatment_limb.map(|limb| limb.slug().to_owned()),
285:             });
286:         }
287:     }
288:     result
289: }

739: fn validate_consequence_order(
740:     order: ConsequenceOrder,
741:     consequences: &[WorldEventConsequence],
742: ) -> Result<(), String> {
743:     match order {
744:         ConsequenceOrder::NoticedIllegalForaging => match consequences {
745:             [
746:                 WorldEventConsequence::Reputation {
747:                     meaning: ReputationMeaning::IllegalForaging,
748:                     character_id: reputation_character,
749:                     settlement_id: reputation_settlement,
750:                     minute: reputation_minute,
751:                     ..
752:                 },
753:                 WorldEventConsequence::DiscoveredOffense {
754:                     kind: ExistingOffenseKind::IllegalForaging,
755:                     character_id: offense_character,
756:                     settlement_id: offense_settlement,
757:                     minute: offense_minute,
758:                     ..
759:                 },
760:             ] if reputation_character == offense_character
761:                 && reputation_settlement == offense_settlement
762:                 && reputation_minute == offense_minute =>
763:             {
764:                 Ok(())
765:             }
766:             _ => Err("Illegal-foraging consequences are not canonical".into()),
767:         },
768:         ConsequenceOrder::GeneratedCaseResolution => {
769:             let consequence_start = usize::from(matches!(
770:                 consequences.first(),
771:                 Some(WorldEventConsequence::LocalProblemOutcome { .. })
772:             ));
773:             let participant_consequences = &consequences[consequence_start..];
774:             if !participant_consequences.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
775:                 return Err("Case-resolution consequences are not canonical".into());
776:             }
777:             let mut prior_character_id = None;
778:             for pair in participant_consequences.as_chunks::<2>().0 {
779:                 let [
780:                     WorldEventConsequence::CaseParticipantSnapshot {
781:                         character_id: snapshot_character,
782:                         case_id,
783:                         ..
784:                     },
785:                     WorldEventConsequence::Reputation {
786:                         meaning: ReputationMeaning::CaseResolution,
787:                         character_id: reputation_character,
788:                         source_id,
789:                         ..
790:                     },
791:                 ] = pair
792:                 else {
793:                     return Err("Case-resolution consequences are not canonical".into());
794:                 };
795:                 if snapshot_character != reputation_character || case_id != source_id {
796:                     return Err("Case-resolution consequence provenance differs".into());
797:                 }
798:                 if prior_character_id.is_some_and(|prior| prior >= *snapshot_character) {
799:                     return Err("Case reputation participants are not canonical".into());
800:                 }
801:                 prior_character_id = Some(*snapshot_character);
802:             }
803:             Ok(())
804:         }
805:         ConsequenceOrder::FoodWaterInfection => match consequences {
806:             [WorldEventConsequence::InfectionEpisode { .. }] => Ok(()),
807:             _ => Err("Food-water infection consequences are not canonical".into()),
808:         },
809:     }
810: }

1: # Fabelgeist tactical client
2: 
3: [Immutable scene preparation](generation.md) describes shared worker products,
4: readiness, residency and typed preparation failures.
5: 
6: [Regional environment presentation](regional-map.md) describes the retained
7: geographic camera, terrain surface and browser command boundary.
8: 
9: The atmosphere extraction backport is required by the selected Bevy 0.19 engine.
10: The build script reads the resolved version from the workspace lockfile and
11: requires removing that backport and its guard when the project selects Bevy 0.20
12: or later. Releasing a new upstream engine does not change the selected engine or
13: make an otherwise unchanged build fail. This check does not access the network.
14: 
15: ## Runtime equipment fitting
16: 
17: Armor and clothing are generated locally from each wearer's evaluated, unposed
18: body. Identity and skeletal fit morphs are evaluated on the body once; skeletal
19: proportion offsets then place its vertices and fitting landmarks. Equipment
20: contains no body-shape morph targets. Its inverse bind poses belong to that
21: wearer's rest skeleton, so animation does not apply proportion changes twice.
22: 
23: The client queues fitting outside frame updates on native builds and awaits
24: WebGPU initialization and readback in the browser. The compute device creates
25: no canvas; Bevy renders the resulting geometry in the existing game canvas.
26: Offline exporters retain their reusable morph-equipped asset workflow.
27: Compute and rendering dependencies must use the same `wgpu` release: linking
28: two releases into the browser client duplicates their vendored WebGPU bindings.
29: 
30: Strategic loading fits the equipment actually requested by the scene. The device
31: and compiled compute kernels stay alive across city travel; loading does not fit
32: and discard the entire authored catalog first. Strategic scene readiness waits
33: for its requested fits, and preparation failures surface as loading errors.
34: Newly encountered wearers receive their own fitted meshes.
35: 
36: Fits are cached by item design, anatomical placement, and evaluated body shape.
37: The last 128 variants remain available across travel; live entities retain their
38: own mesh handles after cache eviction. Changing wearer or proportions requests a
39: new fit. Holding or dropping a previously fitted item preserves its shape and
40: anatomical placement across placeholder rebuilds. Carried and dropped meshes
41: are centered rigid objects; only worn equipment binds to the wearer's skeleton.
42: 
43: Measure fitting separately from rendering with the real canonical body:
44: 
45: ```powershell
46: cargo run -p adventuresim-tactical-client --example runtime_equipment_bench -- assets/animations/biped/unarmed/base.glb 3
47: ```
48: 
49: The JSON records separate device opening, first use, and repeated fits. The
50: vambrace and breastplate comparisons use the same batched readback for one body
51: and the full set of body morph endpoints; they isolate morph generation cost.
52: The browser probe example exercises the same asynchronous runtime generator.
53: Build it with `cargo build -p adventuresim-tactical-client --example
54: armor_browser_probe --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features`.
55: Run the matching `wasm-bindgen` CLI with `--target web` into an output directory,
56: copy `examples/armor_browser_probe.html` there as `index.html`, and copy
57: `assets/animations/biped/unarmed/base.glb` from the repository as `body.glb`.
58: Serve that directory on localhost. The page reports initial preparation time,
59: geometry validity, and first and repeated fitting times for twelve equipment
60: types after preparation. Kernel counts identify any missed first-use work.
61: Gorget and mail-coif section measurements intersect body triangles, so fitting
62: does not require dense vertices near each anatomical measurement plane.
63: 
64: `animation-viewer --armor-harness wearer-fit` renders a gorget, cuirass, and
65: paired vambraces on the actual animated wearer for fitting inspection.
66: Device builders generate pauldrons, wrapped tassets, anime breastplates, and
67: puff-and-slash clothing as well. Unsupported recipes fail readiness instead of
68: loading served equipment meshes or silently substituting another design.
69: 
70: Generated equipment uses ordinary skeletal attachment during animation. Metal
71: parts retain their authored rigid joint ownership; cuirass courses share one
72: chest attachment, and pauldron distal lames follow the upper arm. There is no
73: runtime plate solver, body collision mesh, or per-frame contact search in this
74: generation path. Generation-time layer fitting and closed-shell validation do
75: not establish collision-free animation. Independent plate articulation and
76: contact correction are separate work.
77: 
78: ## Browser release builds
79: 
80: `just build-wasm` keeps the gameplay client on the workspace `release` profile
81: and builds the art demo separately with the size-oriented `wasm-release`
82: profile and no default features. The demo therefore excludes client audio and
83: debug tooling without removing either from ordinary client builds. The build
84: requires the exact `wasm-bindgen` version in `Cargo.lock` and the Binaryen
85: version pinned in the root `package-lock.json`; run `npm ci` to install the
86: latter.
87: 
88: The build applies `wasm-opt -Oz` only to the art demo after `wasm-bindgen` and
89: writes raw, gzip level 6, and Brotli level 11 sizes to
90: `crates/adventuresim-stdb-module/static/wasm/bundle-sizes.json`. In the browser,
91: the developer console's `[art-demo startup]` record separates module download
92: from Wasm compilation and initialization, making a cold-cache startup directly
93: repeatable in browser developer tools.
94: 
95: Outdoor PBR lighting uses Bevy's live atmosphere for sunlight transmission,
96: horizon occlusion, the solar disc and aerial perspective. Generated sky
97: radiance supplies diffuse and specular environment lighting at intensity one;
98: there is no added global ambient visibility floor. The environment map is
99: cached only after GPU completion and invalidated by scene, weather, time,
100: selected atmosphere, its position/scale, or scattering-medium changes. Camera
101: exposure does not invalidate unexposed sky radiance. Probe retirement runs
102: after Bevy's deferred preparation commands. The live atmosphere remains enabled
103: after the environment bake.
104: 
105: The pinned Bevy 0.19.1 atmosphere shaders use local, source-attributed
106: corrections: generation samples texel centres, and the forward/inverse lookup
107: coordinate maps agree. Canonical shader handles and imports stay intact, so
108: visible sky and environment baking use the same mapping. A shader reload
109: invalidates the bake; capture readiness waits for the corrected GPU pipelines.
110: The analytic planet ground samples sunlight transmission at its surface
111: radius, retaining the dependence on solar angle.
112: With multisample anti-aliasing, atmospheric scattering and transmission use
113: each sample's depth and viewport position, so mixed terrain/sky pixels receive
114: the corresponding transport before color resolution.
115: 
116: This environment map samples the atmospheric medium; the separate animated
117: cloud renderer is not included in it. Cloud radiance, cloud beam transmission,
118: and scene bounce lighting require further transport integration. The existing
119: weather source attenuation is an approximation, not a full cloud-scattering
120: solution.
121: 
122: The tactical client renders transient server-authoritative combat state with
123: Bevy. Skeletal animation is presentation-only: the server replicates compact
124: `SkeletonState` posture, locomotion, stance, action, and timing coordinates;
125: the client selects and blends authored poses, then applies procedural look and
126: terrain leg IK.
127: 
128: The equipment HUD shows procedural weapons, holders, and armor as color
129: portraits on black squares. Weapon recipes render into a transient image cache;
130: armor loads the baked portrait for its manifest placement. See the
131: [portrait workflow](../adventuresim-weapon-model/README.md#equipment-portraits)
132: for lighting and regeneration commands.
133: 
134: EGUI renders the centered incapacitation wheel without taking pointer input.
135: The segmented arc surrounds the retained Bevy UI crosshair, starts at 12
136: o'clock, and uses the strategic condition colors for live pain and blood loss
137: plus enrolled fear, fatigue, hunger, thirst, and temperature; tactical
138: imbalance is white. Zero incapacitation draws nothing and a full revolution is
139: the visible maximum.
140: 
141: The gameplay camera is likewise client presentation. A single retained rig
142: blends from centered lowered-guard exploration to raised-guard right-shoulder
143: aiming without smoothing manual yaw or pitch. Focus translation uses bounded
144: anisotropic critical damping and a screen-space sweet spot sized to the current
145: boom distance. A box enclosing the eye and near-plane corners sweeps from the
146: controller center around hard geometry. The final framed position is swept
147: again, so shoulder offsets and focus lag cannot bypass the collision check.
148: Tight spaces blend toward a close shoulder view with a small height offset and
149: reduced focus lag. Collision and close framing are resolved together before
150: recovery, including corners where the close view meets a second obstacle.
151: Retraction is immediate; recovery waits briefly and then uses critical damping
152: and distance hysteresis. Soft occluders remain excluded from camera collision.
153: Raised aiming resolves the center-screen camera target and the subsequent
154: muzzle path separately. Debug builds use `F6` to show rig, collision, smoothing,
155: occlusion classification, and aim-ray telemetry.
156: 
157: Camera frame intervals are capped at 0.1 seconds. Collision hold time is a
158: finite nonnegative interval, including zero, with the existing 0.12-second
159: default. Horizontal and vertical follow, mode-transition and collision-recovery
160: coefficients are finite signed shaping seconds. Profile interpolation precedes
161: the damping equation's existing response floor, so finite zero and negative
162: coefficients retain their behavior. Invalid authored temporal values fail
163: checked admission. Blend and profile results are prepared before replacing
164: their retained filter values; this does not make all camera updates atomic.
165: 
166: The tactical workspace targets Bevy 0.19, Avian 0.7, Ahoy 0.2, Replicon
167: 0.41, Aeronet 0.21, Enhanced Input 0.26, and Flair 0.8. The engine upgrade does
168: not move animation or movement authority: `SkeletonState` and controller state
169: remain server-owned, while authored pose evaluation, lighting, and the Bevy
170: world-asset scene attachment are client presentation. Native and Wasm builds
171: share those semantics through their existing explicit feature sets.
172: 
173: ## Client-generated geological geometry
174: 
175: Collider-bearing rocks replicate compact recipes containing a seed, silhouette
176: archetype, lithology, dimensions, and conservative collision radius. The
177: tactical server creates only the bounded sphere collider and transform. The
178: client samples each recipe on a small uniform grid and extracts its render
179: surface with the private Surface Nets implementation in
180: `src/presentation/volumetric.rs`; it rejects non-finite fields and tests the
181: result for deterministic, outward, closed topology. Loose-stone ground cover
182: reuses four shared client-generated variants without collision or foliage wind.
183: 
184: This extractor is infrastructure for later bounded cliffs, overhangs, and cave
185: patches, not an implemented cave system. Future scene authority must send a
186: compact deterministic field recipe, never a server-generated render mesh.
187: Authored clips are sampled by the client-owned pose buffer. The semantic router
188: reads presentation state, resolves weighted clip samples through the animation
189: pack catalog, and applies fixed-rate FK with per-joint inertialization before

192: Buffered sample counts are distinct from elapsed seconds and absolute ticks;
193: checked interval arithmetic precedes replacement of buffered poses. Inertial
194: clocks retain checked elapsed time while their polynomial kernels keep the

196: Pose buffers distinguish inactive state from retained authored display history.

200: vertical hip correction even at zero elapsed time, then retains that correction
201: on subsequent zero-elapsed observations.

203: Shared semantic evaluation and resolved playback carry the same core

282: 
283: ## Animation export contract
284: 
285: The humanoid base rig is independent from authored motions:
286: 
287: ```text
288: assets/animations/biped/unarmed/base.glb
289: assets/animations/biped/unarmed/walk.glb
290: assets/animations/biped/unarmed/swing.glb
291: assets/animations/biped/unarmed/thrust.glb
292: assets/animations/biped/unarmed/offhand.glb
293: ```
294: 
295: Only `base.glb` supplies a spawnable scene. Its default scene must retain the
296: skinned character mesh; `prepare_rig_base.py` strips only authoring helpers such
297: as the placeholder weapon cylinder. The client attaches this authored scene to
298: both the client-controlled character and replicated remote characters. Each
299: other file contains exactly one coherent motion, named or unnamed, and never
300: has its scene attached. The
301: 30fps `AnimationPackCatalog` explicitly owns every semantic pose through a
302: file/frame anchor and includes unnamed endpoint/closure frames. Source motion
303: files belong under `assets_src/biped/unarmed/`; `assets_src/base.*` remains the
304: rig-source special case until `assets_src/biped/unarmed/base.casc` has a
305: matching
306: base GLB export.
307: 
308: Publish and verify every currently available runtime animation without changing
309: source exports:
310: 
311: ```powershell
312: python scripts/prepare_rig_base.py assets_src/biped/unarmed/base.glb assets/animations/biped/unarmed/base.glb
313: python scripts/prepare_animation_assets.py
314: python scripts/prepare_animation_assets.py --check
315: ```
316: 
317: Motion publication validates the one-animation, duration, and canonical
318: bone-path contracts. Runtime motion GLBs preserve only the canonical hierarchy,
319: bind transforms, and animation data; mesh, skin, material, texture, and image
320: payloads remain solely in the spawnable runtime `base.glb`. The publisher keeps
321: only catalog-addressable frames for ordinary motions, removes tracks that equal
322: the bind transform, and collapses other constant tracks to one key. Walk and run
323: store five cubic anchor keys rather than Cascadeur's exported in-betweens.
324: The `.casc` projects are tracked authoring sources. Their reproducible
325: `assets_src/**/*.glb` exports are ignored; export them locally before publishing
326: the tracked runtime GLBs.
327: 
328: Use these conventions:
329: 
330: - glTF coordinates and meters: +Y up, -Z forward, +X anatomical left;
331: - the scene root stays at the origin and gameplay movement is not baked into it;
332: - the armature bind pose is a T-pose, which is the final runtime fallback;
333: - each motion GLB contains exactly one animation and preserves its documented
334:   semantic anchors;

336:   runtime constructs contact -> passing -> mirrored contact -> mirrored
337:   passing -> contact by sampling the two exact catalog frames on distinct Bevy

339:   poses with linear quarter-cycle weights;

341: - packs in one fallback chain use identical bone names and hierarchy.
342: 
343: Lower-body reflection is evaluated in character space so anatomical left and

700: and the serialized `bars` field.

704: handoff under #765; distinguishing controller missing/blocked outcomes is outside
705: the selected #794 geometry change. Generator admission belongs to #766 and the
706: shared architectural-to-scene conversion belongs to #767.

708: Outdoor furniture arrives as compact immutable recipe references and normal

750: input and scene digest identify the authoritative

2: use anyhow::{Context, Result};
3: use bevy::math::Mat4;
4: pub fn load(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(RuntimeBody, Vec<ForearmMorphSample>)> {
5:     let gltf = gltf::Gltf::from_slice(bytes)?;
6:     let blob = gltf.blob.as_deref().context("expected GLB buffer")?;
7:     let node = gltf
8:         .nodes()
9:         .find(|node| node.skin().is_some() && node.mesh().is_some())
10:         .context("missing body")?;
11:     let skin = node.skin().unwrap();
12:     let mesh = node.mesh().unwrap();
13:     let primitive = mesh.primitives().next().unwrap();
14:     let reader = primitive.reader(|_| Some(blob));
15:     let positions = reader
16:         .read_positions()
17:         .context("positions")?
18:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
19:     let normals = reader
20:         .read_normals()
21:         .context("normals")?
22:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
23:     let indices = reader
24:         .read_indices()
25:         .context("triangles")?
26:         .into_u32()
27:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
28:     let faces = indices.as_chunks::<3>().0.to_vec();
29:     let texcoords = surface_chart(&positions);
30:     let joint_names: fabelgeist_rig::RigJointTable<_> = skin
31:         .joints()
32:         .map(|joint| fabelgeist_rig::RigJointName::from(joint.name().unwrap_or("joint")))
33:         .collect();
34:     let global_joint_states = joint_states(&skin, blob)?;
35:     let rig_joints = joint_names.joint_count();
36:     let morphs = reader
37:         .read_morph_targets()
38:         .enumerate()
39:         .map(|(index, (p, n, _))| ForearmMorphSample {
40:             name: format!("target_{index}"),
41:             positions: positions
42:                 .iter()
43:                 .zip(p.unwrap())
44:                 .map(|(p, d)| std::array::from_fn(|i| p[i] + d[i]))
45:                 .collect(),
46:             normals: n
47:                 .map(|d| {
48:                     normals
49:                         .iter()
50:                         .zip(d)
51:                         .map(|(p, d)| std::array::from_fn(|i| p[i] + d[i]))
52:                         .collect()
53:                 })
54:                 .unwrap_or_else(|| normals.clone()),
55:             global_joint_states: global_joint_states.clone(),
56:             device: Default::default(),
57:         })
58:         .collect();
59:     Ok((
60:         RuntimeBody {
61:             domain: "runtime_body_cylindrical_v1".into(),
62:             positions,
63:             normals,
64:             texcoords,
65:             texcoord_faces: faces.clone(),
66:             faces,
67:             joint_names,
68:             global_joint_states,
69:             joint_indices: fabelgeist_rig::PackedRigSkin::from_native(
70:                 reader
71:                     .read_joints(0)
72:                     .context("joints")?
73:                     .into_u16()
74:                     .map(|j| {
75:                         [
76:                             u32::from(j[0]),
77:                             u32::from(j[1]),
78:                             u32::from(j[2]),
79:                             u32::from(j[3]),
80:                             0,
81:                             0,
82:                             0,
83:                             0,
84:                         ]
85:                     })
86:                     .collect(),
87:                 rig_joints,
88:             )?,
89:             joint_weights: reader
90:                 .read_weights(0)
91:                 .context("weights")?
92:                 .into_f32()
93:                 .map(|w| [w[0], w[1], w[2], w[3], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
94:                 .collect(),
95:             device: Default::default(),
96:         },
97:         morphs,
98:     ))
99: }
100: 
101: fn joint_states(
102:     skin: &gltf::Skin<'_>,
103:     blob: &[u8],
104: ) -> Result<fabelgeist_rig::RigJointTable<[f32; 8]>> {
105:     Ok(skin
106:         .reader(|_| Some(blob))
107:         .read_inverse_bind_matrices()
108:         .context("bind poses")?
109:         .map(|matrix| {
110:             let (scale, rotation, p) = Mat4::from_cols_array_2d(&matrix)
111:                 .inverse()
112:                 .to_scale_rotation_translation();
113:             [
114:                 p.x, p.y, p.z, rotation.x, rotation.y, rotation.z, rotation.w, scale.x,
115:             ]
116:         })
117:         .collect())
118: }
119: 
120: fn surface_chart(positions: &[[f32; 3]]) -> Vec<[f32; 2]> {
121:     let low = positions.iter().map(|p| p[1]).fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
122:     let high = positions
123:         .iter()
124:         .map(|p| p[1])
125:         .fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
126:     positions
127:         .iter()
128:         .map(|[x, y, z]| {
129:             [
130:                 x.atan2(*z) / std::f32::consts::TAU + 0.5,
131:                 (y - low) / (high - low),
132:             ]
133:         })
134:         .collect()
135: }

1: //! Bouncy bones: additive rotational hit springs, client-side.
2: //!
3: //! Impacts kick a per-bone damped rotational spring instead of a ragdoll:
4: //! each reactive bone carries a world-space rotation-vector offset plus
5: //! angular velocity, and a [`BoneKick`] converts a world-space impulse into
6: //! spin on the struck bone (`bone_direction × impulse`: a shove at the tip
7: //! rotates the bone the way the shove points). From there the reaction
8: //! travels the authored chain as a wave: every frame a deflected bone torques
9: //! its parent, so the hand snaps first and the shoulder answers a few frames
10: //! later, cloth-like. Purely cosmetic: nothing syncs and nothing touches
11: //! physics.
12: //!
13: //! The springs advance with the closed-form damped-oscillator solution
14: //! (amplitude and phase, not stepped Euler), so they are unconditionally
15: //! stable at any render delta and tuned in honest units: envelope half-life
16: //! and wobble frequency.
17: //!
18: //! Deltas are applied during a fresh parent-before-child walk of the rig
19: //! with world rotations accumulated on the way down; the cached
20: //! `GlobalTransform` still holds last frame's deltas and would misdirect the
21: //! applied axis.
22: 
23: use adventuresim_core::body::BodyPart;
24: use adventuresim_tactical_core::prelude::*;
25: use bevy::prelude::*;
26: 
27: use super::{
28:     HumanoidBone, HumanoidRig, pose_buffer::PoseBufferRig, procedural::BoneRole,
29:     ragdoll::Ragdolling,
30: };
31: 
32: fn bounce_tuning() -> BouncyBonesConfig {
33:     runtime_animation_config().bouncy_bones
34: }
35: 
36: /// Knock a bone; the chain coupling ripples it toward the pelvis over the
37: /// next frames. `impulse` is a world-space shove at the bone tip in metres
38: /// per second of tip velocity to impart.
39: #[derive(Message, Debug, Clone, Copy)]
40: pub(crate) struct BoneKick {
41:     /// The rig owner (the entity holding [`HumanoidRig`] and [`BouncyBones`]).
42:     pub(crate) owner: Entity,
43:     pub(crate) role: BoneRole,
44:     pub(crate) impulse: Vec3,
45: }
46: 
47: /// The reactive bone a server-reported body-part hit lands on.
48: pub(crate) fn impact_bone_role(part: BodyPart) -> BoneRole {
49:     match part {
50:         BodyPart::Head => BoneRole::Head,
51:         BodyPart::Chest => BoneRole::Chest,
52:         BodyPart::Stomach => BoneRole::StomachTwo,
53:         BodyPart::LeftArm => BoneRole::ForearmLeft,
54:         BodyPart::RightArm => BoneRole::ForearmRight,
55:         BodyPart::LeftLeg => BoneRole::ShinLeft,
56:         BodyPart::RightLeg => BoneRole::ShinRight,
57:     }
58: }
59: 
60: struct ReactiveBone {
61:     role: BoneRole,
62:     /// Index into [`REACTIVE_BONES`] the reaction propagates to next.
63:     parent: Option<usize>,
64:     /// Role whose position marks this bone's tip; `None` extends the line
65:     /// from the chain parent through this bone.
66:     tip: Option<BoneRole>,
67:     /// Inverse-mass feel: how much spin one unit of impulse buys. Hands
68:     /// flap, the pelvis barely nods.
69:     response: f32,
70: }
71: 
72: const fn bone(
73:     role: BoneRole,
74:     parent: Option<usize>,
75:     tip: Option<BoneRole>,
76:     response: f32,
77: ) -> ReactiveBone {
78:     ReactiveBone {
79:         role,
80:         parent,
81:         tip,
82:         response,
83:     }
84: }
85: 
86: /// The reactive skeleton. Parent links are the coupling chain (anatomy, not
87: /// necessarily the exact transform hierarchy). Children inherit their
88: /// parent's wobble through ordinary transform propagation; this chain only
89: /// carries reactions upstream. Feet stay out: the terrain contact solver
90: /// owns them.
91: const REACTIVE_BONES: [ReactiveBone; 19] = [
92:     bone(BoneRole::Pelvis, None, Some(BoneRole::StomachOne), 0.15),
93:     bone(
94:         BoneRole::StomachOne,
95:         Some(0),

113: pub(in crate::animation::procedural) enum QuickstepContactHandoff {

125: 
126: impl QuickstepContactHandoff {
127:     pub(super) fn is_pending(self) -> bool {
128:         matches!(self, Self::Converging { .. })
129:     }
130: 
131:     pub(super) fn is_held(self) -> bool {
132:         matches!(self, Self::Held { .. })
133:     }
134: 
135:     pub(super) fn targets(self) -> Option<(Vec3, Vec3)> {
136:         match self {
137:             Self::None => None,
138:             Self::Converging { left, right } | Self::Held { left, right } => Some((left, right)),
139:         }
140:     }
141: 
142:     pub(super) fn update_targets(&mut self, left: Vec3, right: Vec3) {
143:         *self = match self {
144:             Self::Converging { .. } => Self::Converging { left, right },
145:             Self::Held { .. } => Self::Held { left, right },
146:             Self::None => Self::None,
147:         };
148:     }
149: 
150:     pub(super) fn hold(&mut self) {
151:         if let Self::Converging { left, right } = *self {
152:             *self = Self::Held { left, right };
153:         }
154:     }
155: }

157: pub(in crate::animation::procedural) fn seed_quickstep_contact_handoff(
158:     memory: &mut LegIkMemory,
159:     frame: ObservedRigFrame,
160:     left_world: Vec3,
161:     right_world: Vec3,
162: ) -> bool {
163:     if !left_world.is_finite() || !right_world.is_finite() {
164:         return false;
165:     }
166:     let (rig_origin, rig_rotation) = (frame.origin(), frame.rotation());
167:     let inverse_rotation = rig_rotation.inverse();
168:     let left = inverse_rotation * (left_world - rig_origin);
169:     let right = inverse_rotation * (right_world - rig_origin);
170:     if !left.is_finite() || !right.is_finite() {
171:         return false;
172:     }
173:     memory.quickstep_handoff = QuickstepContactHandoff::Converging { left, right };
174:     memory.owner_frame = Some(frame);
175:     true
176: }

45: pub(in crate::animation::procedural) fn uses_run_airborne_motion_budget(

52:                 .reference_speed

184:     retained_speed: Option<NonnegativeSpeed>,
185:     previous_origin: Option<Vec3>,
186:     current_origin: Vec3,
187:     delta_seconds: AnimationElapsed,
188:     evaluation_advances: bool,
189:     owner_discontinuous: bool,
190: ) -> AnimationValueResult<Option<NonnegativeSpeed>> {
191:     if !evaluation_advances {
192:         Ok(retained_speed)
193:     } else if owner_discontinuous || delta_seconds.is_zero() {
194:         Ok(None)
195:     } else {
196:         previous_origin
197:             .map(|previous| {
198:                 NonnegativeSpeed::from_metres_per_second(
199:                     current_origin.xz().distance(previous.xz()) / delta_seconds.seconds(),
200:                 )

203:                 })

210:     phase: CyclePhase,

212:     support_radius: CycleDelta,
213: ) -> bool {
214:     let support_radius = support_radius.cycles();
215:     let post_contact = phase.since_contact(foot_side).cycles();
216:     // Release on the first sampled phase beyond the nominal lobe, not on its
217:     // decaying shoulder. The half-cycle bound distinguishes this foot's
218:     // post-contact side from its next rising shoulder after wrap.
219:     post_contact >= support_radius && post_contact < 0.5
220: }

222: pub(in crate::animation::procedural) fn exhausted_latch_after_raw_cadence(
223:     exhausted: bool,
224:     raw_nominal_support: UnitInterval,
225: ) -> bool {
226:     // Exhaustion suppresses only the remainder of the current support lobe.
227:     // Consult the unsuppressed gait cadence here: reported/effective support
228:     // may be zero precisely because this latch is active and therefore cannot
229:     // prove that the foot has crossed true flight into its next cycle.
230:     exhausted && terrain_leg_has_support(raw_nominal_support)

55:     pub(crate) fn admit(name: &ScenarioMetadata<'_>, kind: ScenarioKind) -> Self {

57:         let raised_stop = name.has(ScenarioFeature::RaisedTapStop);
58:         let named = name.has(ScenarioFeature::TerrainNamed);
59:         if toggle {
60:             Self::Toggle
61:         } else if raised_stop {
62:             Self::RaisedStop {
63:                 startup: if named {
64:                     TerrainIkMode::Enabled
65:                 } else {
66:                     TerrainIkMode::Disabled
67:                 },
68:             }

71:         } else if named {

73:         } else {
74:             Self::Absent

81:             Self::RaisedStop { startup } => startup,
82:             Self::Authored | Self::Named | Self::Toggle => TerrainIkMode::Enabled,
83:         }

107:     identity: Option<ScenarioId>,
108:     features: BTreeSet<ScenarioFeature>,

110:     let name = ScenarioMetadata {
111:         label,
112:         identity,
113:         features,
114:         terrain: ScenarioTerrain::Absent,
115:         kind: ScenarioKind::Ordinary,
116:         repeatable: Repeatability::Repeating,
117:         procedural_solver: SolverUse::Authored,
118:         execution: ScenarioExecution::default(),
119:     };
120:     let classified = |kind, repeatable, procedural_solver| ScenarioMetadata {
121:         label: name.label.clone(),
122:         identity: name.identity,
123:         features: name.features.clone(),
124:         terrain: ScenarioTerrain::admit(&name, kind),
125:         kind,
126:         execution: ScenarioExecution {
127:             body: downed_body_for_scenario(&name),
128:             motion: required_motion_for_scenario(&name),
129:             transition: transition_for_scenario(&name),
130:         },
131:         repeatable: if repeatable {
132:             Repeatability::Repeating
133:         } else {
134:             Repeatability::Transition
135:         },
136:         procedural_solver: if procedural_solver {
137:             SolverUse::Procedural
138:         } else {
139:             SolverUse::Authored
140:         },
141:     };
142:     if is_quickstep_scenario(&name)
143:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::Downed)
144:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::Dive)
145:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::GetUp)
146:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::ProneRoll)
147:         || name.is(ScenarioId::JumpChargeAnticipation)
148:     {
149:         classified(ScenarioKind::Transition, false, false)
150:     } else if name.is(ScenarioId::TerrainToggleMidStride) {
151:         classified(
152:             ScenarioKind::Terrain,
153:             false, // contract is bounded transition continuity, not steady plants.
154:             false,
155:         )
156:     } else if matches!(
157:         name.identity,
158:         Some(ScenarioId::FlatGridWalkNoIk) | Some(ScenarioId::FlatGridSprintNoIk)
159:     ) {
160:         classified(ScenarioKind::Ordinary, true, false)
161:     } else if name.is(ScenarioId::CrossSlopeWalk)
162:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::TerrainPrefix)
163:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::FlatGrid)
164:     {
165:         classified(
166:             ScenarioKind::Terrain,
167:             !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Stop)
168:                 && !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Turn)
169:                 && !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Toggle)
170:                 && !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Restart)
171:                 && !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Chatter)
172:                 && !name.has(ScenarioFeature::TerrainSteadyRun),
173:             true,
174:         )
175:     } else if name.has(ScenarioFeature::AttackLive) {
176:         classified(ScenarioKind::Attack, false, true)
177:     } else if name.has(ScenarioFeature::RaisedGuard) {
178:         classified(
179:             ScenarioKind::RaisedGuard,
180:             !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Release)
181:                 && !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Reversal)
182:                 && !name.has(ScenarioFeature::Accelerate)
183:                 && !name.is(ScenarioId::RaisedGuardStationaryTurn)
184:                 && !name.is(ScenarioId::RaisedGuardTransition), // procedural plant/step solver.
185:             !uses_authored_combat_locomotion(&name),
186:         )
187:     } else if name.is(ScenarioId::AirborneLanding) {
188:         classified(ScenarioKind::Landing, false, false)
189:     } else if name.has(ScenarioFeature::Transition)
190:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::EnterExit)
191:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::HardStop)
192:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::Ramp)
193:         || name.has(ScenarioFeature::Turn)
194:     {
195:         classified(ScenarioKind::Transition, false, false)
196:     } else {

198:     }

201: fn downed_body_for_scenario(scenario: &ScenarioMetadata<'_>) -> Option<BodyState> {
202:     match scenario.identity {
203:         Some(ScenarioId::DownedProneCrawl) | Some(ScenarioId::DownedProneLookAt) => {
204:             Some(BodyState::Prone)
205:         }
206:         Some(ScenarioId::DownedSupineScamper) => Some(BodyState::Supine),
207:         Some(ScenarioId::FullRagdoll) => Some(BodyState::Ragdolled),
208:         _ => None,
209:     }

212: fn required_motion_for_scenario(
213:     scenario: &ScenarioMetadata<'_>,
214: ) -> Option<crate::animation::MotionId> {
215:     if scenario.has(ScenarioFeature::Dive) {
216:         return Some(crate::animation::MotionId::DIVE);
217:     }
218:     match scenario.identity {
219:         Some(ScenarioId::DownedProneCrawl) => Some(crate::animation::MotionId::PRONE_CRAWL),
220:         Some(ScenarioId::DownedSupineScamper) => Some(crate::animation::MotionId::SUPINE_SCAMPER),
221:         Some(ScenarioId::DownedProneLookAt) => Some(crate::animation::MotionId::PRONE_IDLE),
222:         Some(ScenarioId::ProneGetUp) => Some(crate::animation::MotionId::PRONE_TRANSITION),
223:         Some(ScenarioId::SupineGetUp) => Some(crate::animation::MotionId::SUPINE_TRANSITION),
224:         Some(ScenarioId::ProneRollLeft) => Some(crate::animation::MotionId::PRONE_SUPINE_ROLL_LEFT),
225:         Some(ScenarioId::ProneRollRight) => {
226:             Some(crate::animation::MotionId::PRONE_SUPINE_ROLL_RIGHT)
227:         }
228:         _ => None,
229:     }
230: }

232: fn transition_for_scenario(
233:     scenario: &ScenarioMetadata<'_>,
234: ) -> Option<(BodyState, PostureTransitionKind)> {
235:     let upright = BodyState::Grounded(GroundedPosture::Upright);
236:     let dive_direction = if scenario.has(ScenarioFeature::DiveForward) {
237:         Some(DiveDirection::Forward)
238:     } else if scenario.has(ScenarioFeature::DiveBackward) {
239:         Some(DiveDirection::Backward)
240:     } else if scenario.has(ScenarioFeature::DiveLeft) {
241:         Some(DiveDirection::Left)
242:     } else if scenario.has(ScenarioFeature::DiveRight) {
243:         Some(DiveDirection::Right)
244:     } else {
245:         None
246:     };
247:     if let Some(direction) = dive_direction {
248:         return Some((
249:             upright,
250:             PostureTransitionKind::DiveToDowned {
251:                 direction,
252:                 trajectory: DiveTrajectory::Airborne,
253:             },
254:         ));
255:     }
256:     match scenario.identity {
257:         Some(ScenarioId::ProneGetUp) => {
258:             Some((BodyState::Prone, PostureTransitionKind::ProneToUpright))
259:         }
260:         Some(ScenarioId::SupineGetUp) => {
261:             Some((BodyState::Supine, PostureTransitionKind::SupineToUpright))
262:         }
263:         Some(ScenarioId::ProneRollLeft) => Some((
264:             BodyState::Prone,
265:             PostureTransitionKind::ProneToSupine {
266:                 direction: RollDirection::Left,
267:             },
268:         )),
269:         Some(ScenarioId::ProneRollRight) => Some((
270:             BodyState::Prone,
271:             PostureTransitionKind::ProneToSupine {
272:                 direction: RollDirection::Right,
273:             },
274:         )),
275:         _ => None,
276:     }
277: }

352: mod tests {
353:     use std::{fs, path::Path};
354: 
355:     /// WGSL requires every directive to precede the first declaration, and an
356:     /// `#import` expands into declarations. A directive written below the
357:     /// imports fails composition for the whole file, which surfaces only as a
358:     /// log line while the material stops rendering on every backend.
359:     #[test]
360:     fn shader_directives_precede_declarations() {
361:         // Both shader roots the tactical renderer composes: the runtime asset
362:         // directory and the shaders embedded in the procedural materials crate.
363:         const SHADER_ROOTS: [&str; 2] = [
364:             concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../assets/shaders"),
365:             concat!(
366:                 env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
367:                 "/../adventuresim-procedural-materials/src/shaders"
368:             ),
369:         ];
370:         let mut checked = 0;
371:         for root in SHADER_ROOTS {
372:             for entry in fs::read_dir(Path::new(root)).expect("tactical shader directory") {
373:                 let path = entry.expect("shader directory entry").path();
374:                 if path.extension().is_none_or(|extension| extension != "wgsl") {
375:                     continue;
376:                 }
377:                 let source = fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("readable tactical shader");
378:                 assert_directives_precede_declarations(&path.display().to_string(), &source);
379:                 checked += 1;
380:             }
381:         }
382:         assert!(checked > 0, "no tactical shaders were checked");
383:     }
384: 
385:     fn assert_directives_precede_declarations(label: &str, source: &str) {
386:         let mut declared = false;
387:         for (index, line) in source.lines().enumerate() {
388:             let line = line.trim();
389:             if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with("//") {
390:                 continue;
391:             }
392:             if line.starts_with("diagnostic(")
393:                 || line.starts_with("enable ")
394:                 || line.starts_with("requires ")
395:             {
396:                 assert!(
397:                     !declared,
398:                     "{label}:{}: WGSL directive written after a declaration; \
399:                      move it above the imports or the shader will not compile",
400:                     index + 1
401:                 );
402:             } else if !line.starts_with('#') || line.starts_with("#import") {
403:                 declared = true;
404:             }
405:         }
406:     }
407: }

259: /// effect depend on the representative path length through each crown. The
260: /// extinction is deliberately bounded below dense-forest values because the
261: /// explicit leaf cards and screen-space AO already resolve part of the crown's
262: /// self-occlusion.

1: //! Converts compact geological recipes into the terrain extension's cliff uniforms.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: use adventuresim_world_schema::BASIS_POINTS_PER_WHOLE;
5: 
6: const TERRAIN_SHADER: &str = "shaders/tactical_terrain.wgsl";
7: 
8: /// Flat Bevy binding shared by ordinary terrain and the implicit cliff patch.
9: /// Cliff uniforms and textures live here beside the pre-existing terrain
10: /// fields because one material extension owns binding group 100.
11: #[derive(Asset, AsBindGroup, Reflect, Debug, Clone)]
12: pub(in crate::presentation) struct TacticalTerrainExtension {
13:     #[uniform(100)]
14:     pub(super) base_color: Vec4,
15:     #[uniform(100)]
16:     pub(super) grass_color: Vec4,
17:     #[uniform(100)]
18:     pub(super) cover: Vec4,
19:     #[uniform(100)]
20:     pub(super) weather: Vec4,
21:     #[uniform(100)]
22:     pub(super) far_sward: Vec4,
23:     #[uniform(100)]
24:     pub(super) lod_sward: Vec4,
25:     #[uniform(100)]
26:     pub(super) playable_bounds: Vec4,
27:     #[uniform(100)]
28:     pub(super) detail_patch: Vec4,
29:     #[uniform(100)]
30:     pub(super) soil_detail: Vec4,
31:     #[uniform(100)]
32:     pub(super) litter_detail: Vec4,
33:     #[uniform(100)]
34:     pub(super) cliff_palette_a: Vec4,
35:     #[uniform(100)]
36:     pub(super) cliff_palette_b: Vec4,
37:     #[uniform(100)]
38:     pub(super) cliff_surface: Vec4,
39:     #[uniform(100)]
40:     pub(super) cliff_structure_a: Vec4,
41:     #[uniform(100)]
42:     pub(super) cliff_structure_b: Vec4,
43:     #[uniform(100)]
44:     pub(super) source_from_world: Mat4,
45:     #[texture(101)]
46:     #[sampler(102)]
47:     pub(super) ground_map: Handle<Image>,
48:     #[texture(103)]
49:     #[sampler(104)]
50:     pub(super) soil_height_ao: Handle<Image>,
51:     #[texture(105)]
52:     #[sampler(106)]
53:     pub(super) litter_surface: Handle<Image>,
54:     // Both litter maps share filtering and addressing; reuse binding 106.
55:     #[texture(107)]
56:     pub(super) litter_normal: Handle<Image>,
57:     #[texture(109)]
58:     #[sampler(110)]
59:     pub(super) blood_mask: Handle<Image>,
60:     #[texture(111)]
61:     #[sampler(112)]
62:     pub(super) cliff_height: Handle<Image>,
63:     // Rock height and ARM share filtering and addressing; reuse binding 112.
64:     #[texture(113)]
65:     pub(super) cliff_arm: Handle<Image>,
66: }
67: 
68: impl TacticalTerrainExtension {
69:     /// Native shader adapter: material coordinates retain canonical city metres
70:     /// while the map window moves. Static map ground has no camera detail cutout.
71:     pub(in crate::presentation) fn set_geographic_frame(
72:         &mut self,
73:         frame: super::super::buildings::CityFrame,
74:     ) {
75:         self.source_from_world = frame.world_from_city().inverse();
76:         self.detail_patch.x = 0.0;
77:     }
78: }
79: 
80: impl MaterialExtension for TacticalTerrainExtension {
81:     fn fragment_shader() -> ShaderRef {
82:         TERRAIN_SHADER.into()
83:     }
84: 
85:     fn deferred_fragment_shader() -> ShaderRef {
86:         TERRAIN_SHADER.into()
87:     }
88: }
89: 
90: pub(in crate::presentation) type TacticalTerrainMaterial =
91:     ExtendedMaterial<StandardMaterial, TacticalTerrainExtension>;
92: 
93: pub(in crate::presentation) fn enable_cliff_surface(
94:     material: &mut TacticalTerrainMaterial,
95:     recipe: TerrainSurfaceRecipe,
96: ) {
97:     let parameters = recipe.parameters();
98:     let palette = parameters.palette_srgb.map(|rgb| {
99:         Color::srgb_u8(rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2])
100:             .to_linear()
101:             .to_f32_array()
102:     });
103:     material.extension.cliff_palette_a =
104:         Vec4::new(palette[0][0], palette[0][1], palette[0][2], 1.0);
105:     material.extension.cliff_palette_b =
106:         Vec4::new(palette[1][0], palette[1][1], palette[1][2], 0.0);
107:     material.extension.cliff_surface = Vec4::new(
108:         1.0 / parameters.grain_tile_metres,
109:         parameters.microrelief_metres,
110:         parameters.roughness[0],
111:         parameters.roughness[1],
112:     );
113:     let basis_points_per_whole = f32::from(BASIS_POINTS_PER_WHOLE);
114:     let (normal, mode, structure) = match recipe.structure() {
115:         TerrainGeologicStructure::Massive => ([0.0, 1.0, 0.0], 0.0, Vec4::ZERO),
116:         TerrainGeologicStructure::Bedded {
117:             normal_permyriad,
118:             bed_thickness_cm,
119:             thickness_variation_bps,
120:             warp_cm,
121:             cross_bedding_bps,
122:         } => (
123:             normal_permyriad.map(|value| f32::from(value) / basis_points_per_whole),
124:             1.0,
125:             Vec4::new(
126:                 f32::from(bed_thickness_cm) / 100.0,
127:                 f32::from(thickness_variation_bps) / basis_points_per_whole,
128:                 f32::from(warp_cm) / 100.0,
129:                 f32::from(cross_bedding_bps) / basis_points_per_whole,
130:             ),
131:         ),
132:         TerrainGeologicStructure::Foliated {
133:             normal_permyriad,
134:             band_spacing_cm,
135:             warp_cm,
136:         } => (
137:             normal_permyriad.map(|value| f32::from(value) / basis_points_per_whole),
138:             2.0,
139:             Vec4::new(
140:                 f32::from(band_spacing_cm) / 100.0,
141:                 0.22,
142:                 f32::from(warp_cm) / 100.0,
143:                 0.0,
144:             ),
145:         ),
146:     };
147:     material.extension.cliff_structure_a = Vec4::new(normal[0], normal[1], normal[2], mode);
148:     material.extension.cliff_structure_b = structure;
149: }
150: 
151: #[cfg(test)]
152: mod tests {
153:     use super::*;
154:     use adventuresim_world_schema::{IgneousRock, SedimentaryRock, SurfaceLithology};
155: 
156:     #[test]
157:     fn ordinary_terrain_disables_cliff_and_patch_recipe_enables_it() {
158:         let mut images = Assets::<Image>::default();
159:         let procedural_assets = generate_procedural_textures(
160:             &adventuresim_procedural_textures::TextureParameters::default(),
161:             &mut images,
162:         );
163:         // Sharing these samplers keeps the full terrain pipeline within WebGPU's
164:         // sixteen-sampler limit without changing filtering or wrap behavior.
165:         for (sampled, shared) in [
166:             (
167:                 &procedural_assets.forest_soil.litter_normal,
168:                 &procedural_assets.forest_soil.litter_surface,
169:             ),
170:             (&procedural_assets.rock.arm, &procedural_assets.rock.height),
171:         ] {
172:             assert_eq!(
173:                 images.get(sampled).unwrap().sampler,
174:                 images.get(shared).unwrap().sampler
175:             );
176:         }
177:         let terrain = SceneTerrain::new(8, 8, 1.0, |_| 0.0).unwrap();
178:         let environment = SceneEnvironmentFixture::TemperateHills.snapshot("cliff-material");
179:         let graphics = TacticalGraphicsSettings::default();
180:         let mut material = terrain_material(
181:             &terrain,
182:             &environment,
183:             None,
184:             &procedural_assets,
185:             &mut images,
186:             &graphics.config.grass,
187:         )
188:         .unwrap();
189:         assert_eq!(material.extension.cliff_palette_a.w, 0.0);
190: 
191:         let sandstone = TerrainSurfaceRecipe::new(
192:             SurfaceLithology::Sedimentary(SedimentaryRock::Sandstone),
193:             TerrainSurfaceSource::AuthoredFixture,
194:             47_115.into(),
195:             [10_000, 0],
196:         )
197:         .unwrap();
198:         enable_cliff_surface(&mut material, sandstone);
199:         assert_eq!(material.extension.cliff_palette_a.w, 1.0);
200:         assert_eq!(material.extension.cliff_structure_a.w, 1.0);
201:         assert_ne!(
202:             material.extension.cliff_palette_a.xyz(),
203:             material.extension.cliff_palette_b.xyz()
204:         );
205: 
206:         let granite = TerrainSurfaceRecipe::new(
207:             SurfaceLithology::Igneous(IgneousRock::Granite),
208:             TerrainSurfaceSource::AuthoredFixture,
209:             47_117.into(),
210:             [10_000, 0],
211:         )
212:         .unwrap();
213:         enable_cliff_surface(&mut material, granite);
214:         assert_eq!(material.extension.cliff_structure_a.w, 0.0);
215:     }
216: }

1: //! Landform ownership must also survive clipping into distant terrain rings.
2: use super::*;
3: use adventuresim_world_schema::{SedimentaryRock, SurfaceLithology};
4: use std::collections::BTreeSet;
5: 
6: type TriangleBits = [[u32; 3]; 3];
7: 
8: fn triangle_bits(triangle: [Vec3; 3]) -> TriangleBits {
9:     triangle.map(|point| point.to_array().map(f32::to_bits))
10: }
11: 
12: fn mesh_triangles(mesh: &Mesh) -> BTreeSet<TriangleBits> {
13:     let positions = mesh
14:         .attribute(Mesh::ATTRIBUTE_POSITION)
15:         .unwrap()
16:         .as_float3()
17:         .unwrap();
18:     let indices = mesh.indices().unwrap().iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
19:     indices
20:         .as_chunks::<3>()
21:         .0
22:         .iter()
23:         .map(|indices| triangle_bits(indices.map(|index| Vec3::from_array(positions[index]))))
24:         .collect()
25: }
26: 
27: #[test]
28: fn landform_cutout_crossing_playable_boundary_retains_distant_foundation_bearings() {
29:     let input = TacticalSceneInput::load(std::path::Path::new(concat!(
30:         env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
31:         "/../../assets/tactical-scenes/facade-review.json"
32:     )))
33:     .unwrap();
34:     let terrain = input
35:         .generate_unfurnished(Default::default())
36:         .unwrap()
37:         .terrain;
38:     let recipe = TerrainLandformRecipe::from_quantized(
39:         adventuresim_tactical_core::volumetric_terrain::QuantizedLandformRecipe {
40:             kind: TerrainLandformKind::FaultScarp,
41:             surface: TerrainSurfaceRecipe::new(
42:                 SurfaceLithology::Sedimentary(SedimentaryRock::Sandstone),
43:                 TerrainSurfaceSource::AuthoredFixture,
44:                 17.into(),
45:                 [10_000, 0],
46:             )
47:             .unwrap(),
48:             seed: 17.into(),
49:             origin_cm: [0, 0],
50:             tangent_permyriad: [10_000, 0],
51:             relief_cm: 600,
52:             half_length_cm: 1_200,
53:             half_width_cm: 1_000,
54:             collar_cm: 250,
55:             lod: TerrainLandformLod::Detail,
56:         },
57:     )
58:     .unwrap();
59:     let collar = recipe.transition_collar();
60:     let source = terrain.property_surface().unwrap();
61:     let removed: BTreeSet<_> = source
62:         .natural_triangles()
63:         .iter()
64:         .filter(|triangle| {
65:             adventuresim_tactical_core::scene_coordinates::ScenePlanPoint::try_from(
66:                 (triangle.iter().copied().sum::<Vec3>() / 3.0).xz(),
67:             )
68:             .is_ok_and(|point| collar.cuts_out(point))
69:         })
70:         .map(|[a, b, c]| triangle_bits([*a, *c, *b]))
71:         .collect();
72:     let bearings: BTreeSet<_> = source
73:         .foundations()
74:         .iter()
75:         .flat_map(|foundation| {
76:             foundation.support_triangles().iter().map(|indices| {
77:                 triangle_bits(indices.map(|index| foundation.positions()[index as usize]))
78:             })
79:         })
80:         .collect();
81:     let lod = VistaLod {
82:         level: adventuresim_tactical_core::scene_input::VistaLevelIndex::new(0),
83:         width: 9,
84:         depth: 9,
85:         spacing_metres: 50.0,
86:         origin_east_metres: 0.0,
87:         origin_north_metres: 0.0,
88:         heights_metres: vec![0.0; 81],
89:         environment: vec![Default::default(); 81],
90:     };
91:     let ring_triangles = |collar| {
92:         vista_meshes(
93:             terrain.property_surface().unwrap(),
94:             &lod,
95:             Vec2::splat(1.0),
96:             None,
97:             None,
98:             input.environment_snapshot("owned-ring".into()).weather,
99:             collar,
100:         )
101:         .unwrap()
102:         .iter()
103:         .flat_map(mesh_triangles)
104:         .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
105:     };
106:     let uncut = ring_triangles(None);
107:     assert!(
108:         !uncut.is_disjoint(&removed),
109:         "fixture must exercise natural cutout faces in the ring"
110:     );
111:     let cut = ring_triangles(Some(collar));
112:     assert!(cut.is_disjoint(&removed));
113:     assert!(
114:         !bearings.is_disjoint(&uncut),
115:         "fixture must exercise distant foundation bearings"
116:     );
117:     assert!(bearings.intersection(&uncut).all(|face| cut.contains(face)));
118: }

221: fn weather_surface<'a>(
222:     terrain: Option<&'a SceneTerrain>,
223:     backdrop: Option<&'a StrategicBackdrop>,
224: ) -> Option<&'a SceneTerrain> {
225:     match (terrain, backdrop) {

227:         (None, Some(backdrop)) => Some(backdrop.weather_surface()),
228:         _ => None,
229:     }

232: fn weather_material(
233:     environment: &SceneEnvironment,
234:     terrain: &SceneTerrain,
235:     range: SceneElevationRange,
236:     heightmap: Handle<Image>,
237:     occlusion_map: Handle<Image>,
238:     layer: WeatherParticle,
239: ) -> TacticalWeatherMaterial {
240:     let kind = match (environment.weather.precipitation, layer) {
241:         (Precipitation::Rain, WeatherParticle::Falling) => 1.0,
242:         (Precipitation::Snow, WeatherParticle::Falling) => 2.0,
243:         (Precipitation::Rain, WeatherParticle::Impact) => 3.0,
244:         (Precipitation::Rain, WeatherParticle::DistantSheet) => 4.0,
245:         _ => 0.0,
246:     };
247:     let bearing = f32::from(environment.weather.atmosphere.wind_direction_degrees).to_radians();

271:             range.minimum().metres(),
272:             range.maximum().metres(),
273:         ),
274:         heightmap,
275:         occlusion_map,
276:     }
277: }

2: use bevy::{camera::Exposure, ecs::system::SystemParam, prelude::*};
3: use serde::Serialize;
4:

7:     position: Vec3,
8:     exposure_ev100: f32,
9:     camera_daylight: Vec3,
10:     subject_daylight: Vec3,
11: }
12: 
13: #[derive(SystemParam)]
14: pub(super) struct LightingDiagnostics<'w, 's> {
15:     pub gpu: Res<'w, crate::presentation::interior_lighting::InteriorLightingGpu>,
16:     cameras: Query<
17:         'w,
18:         's,
19:         (&'static Camera, &'static GlobalTransform, &'static Exposure),
20:         With<super::views::StrategicCamera>,
21:     >,
22: }
23: 
24: impl LightingDiagnostics<'_, '_> {
25:     pub fn views(&self) -> Vec<ViewLighting> {
26:         self.cameras
27:             .iter()
28:             .filter(|(camera, ..)| camera.is_active)
29:             .map(|(_, transform, exposure)| ViewLighting {
30:                 position: transform.translation(),
31:                 exposure_ev100: exposure.ev100,
32:                 camera_daylight: self.gpu.sample_at(transform.translation()),
33:                 subject_daylight: self.gpu.sample_at(
34:                     transform.translation()

36:                 ),

38:             .collect()

Resident LOD mask: `{:#08b}`.\n",

    fs::write(output.join("scene-performance-comparison.md"), markdown)
        .expect("scene performance benchmark table writes");
}

impl TerrainSummary {
    pub(super) fn new(
        input: &adventuresim_tactical_core::prelude::TacticalSceneInput,
        terrain: &adventuresim_tactical_core::prelude::SceneTerrain,
    ) -> TerrainSupportResult<Self> {
        let bounds = terrain.required_elevation_range()?;
        Ok(Self {
            width_metres: terrain.width(),
            depth_metres: terrain.depth(),
            source_spacing_metres: input.playable.spacing_metres,
            spacing_metres: terrain.grid_scale(),
            source_samples: input.playable.heights_metres.len(),
            generated_samples: terrain.grid_width() * terrain.grid_depth(),
            minimum_height_metres: bounds.minimum(),
            maximum_height_metres: bounds.maximum(),
        })
    }
}

        mut self,
        captures: &[CaptureRecord],
        views: &[CaptureViewSpec],
    ) -> (SceneCaptureManifest, bool) {
        self.manifest.captures.clone_from_slice(captures);
        finalize_screenshot_validation(
            &self.manifest.fixture,
            &self.manifest.capture_profile,

            &mut self.manifest.validation,
            &self.manifest.captures,
            views,
        );
        let valid = self.manifest.validation.passed;
        (self.manifest, valid)
    }
}

39:             let tree = tree.metres();

41:             // Frame both current mature-tree presentations, including the

46:                 Position::from_metres(

66:                 Position::from_metres(tree + Vec3::new(8.0, 4.5, 8.0))?,

5: pub(super) fn vista_valley(

13:         .try_normalize()

2: 
3: /// Selects the in-range candidate closest to the camera's forward axis.
4: /// Distance only breaks equal cursor alignment, matching ground-item auto aim.
5: pub(crate) fn auto_aim_candidate<T: Copy>(
6:     camera_origin: Vec3,
7:     camera_forward: Vec3,
8:     actor_origin: Vec3,
9:     maximum_distance: f32,
10:     candidates: impl IntoIterator<Item = (T, Vec3, u64)>,
11: ) -> Option<T> {
12:     let camera_forward = camera_forward.try_normalize()?;
13:     let maximum_distance_squared = maximum_distance.max(0.0).powi(2);
14:     candidates
15:         .into_iter()
16:         .filter_map(|(candidate, position, stable_key)| {
17:             let actor_distance_squared = position.distance_squared(actor_origin);
18:             if actor_distance_squared > maximum_distance_squared {
19:                 return None;
20:             }
21:             let alignment = (position - camera_origin)
22:                 .try_normalize()
23:                 .map_or(-1.0, |direction| direction.dot(camera_forward));
24:             let angular_error = 1.0 - alignment.clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
25:             Some((candidate, angular_error, actor_distance_squared, stable_key))
26:         })
27:         .min_by(|left, right| {
28:             left.1
29:                 .total_cmp(&right.1)
30:                 .then(left.2.total_cmp(&right.2))
31:                 .then(left.3.cmp(&right.3))
32:         })
33:         .map(|(candidate, _, _, _)| candidate)
34: }

# Tactical gameplay mechanics guide

## Authored runtime parameters

`content/tactical/combat.yaml` is the canonical authored source for tactical
combat and animation tuning. Always place a new combat, movement, targeting,
impact-response, or animation tuning parameter in that YAML and represent it
as a typed field in `src/combat_config.rs`. Validate its physical range, keep
the Rust default exactly synchronized with the committed YAML, and carry the
server-loaded snapshot to every runtime consumer that needs the value.

Do not introduce a production numeric, boolean, duration, threshold, scale, or
mode constant as a substitute for a combat-YAML field. Compile-time structural
invariants, protocol limits, and mathematical identities may remain in code.
When shared core combat or autoresolve needs a configured value, pass a typed
projection into the shared calculation rather than duplicating a default or
reading mutable global state.

1: //! Leg-scaled guard stance and contact travel in rig-local metres.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: use adventuresim_building_generator::spatial_geometry::SignedLength;
5: 
6: // Measured hip-knee-ankle chain of the current humanoid rig. The animation
7: // client uses its live rig measurement; this is the server-side fallback until
8: // anatomical dimensions become part of character state.
9: /// Ground distance covered by one procedural combat-stance contact interval.
10: pub fn guard_step_length() -> AnimationValueResult<NonnegativeLength> {
11:     guard_contact_travel_distance(
12:         guard_footwork_config().reference_leg_length_metres.into(),
13:         Vec2::NEG_Y,
14:     )
15: }
16: 
17: /// Maximum lateral open stance. Like the longitudinal opening, this is the
18: /// leg-length-scaled one-yard reference stance: the moving-side foot reaches
19: /// outward while the support foot remains behind the projected COM.
20: pub fn guard_maximum_lateral_foot_separation(
21:     leg_length: SignedLength,
22: ) -> AnimationValueResult<NonnegativeLength> {
23:     guard_maximum_foot_separation(leg_length)
24: }
25: 
26: /// Direction-specific open stance, blended continuously for diagonals.
27: pub fn guard_open_foot_separation(
28:     leg_length: SignedLength,
29:     local_direction: Vec2,
30: ) -> AnimationValueResult<NonnegativeLength> {
31:     let direction = local_direction.normalize_or_zero();
32:     let longitudinal = direction.y.abs();
33:     NonnegativeLength::from_arithmetic(
34:         guard_maximum_lateral_foot_separation(leg_length)?
35:             .metres()
36:             .lerp(
37:                 guard_maximum_foot_separation(leg_length)?.metres(),
38:                 longitudinal,
39:             ),
40:     )
41: }
42: 
43: /// Direction-specific closed stance. Lateral shuffles retain normal
44: /// anatomical width; the three-inch contract applies along the guard's
45: /// longitudinal axis.
46: pub fn guard_closed_foot_separation(
47:     leg_length: SignedLength,
48:     local_direction: Vec2,
49: ) -> AnimationValueResult<NonnegativeLength> {
50:     let direction = local_direction.normalize_or_zero();
51:     let longitudinal = direction.y.abs();
52:     NonnegativeLength::from_arithmetic((leg_length.metres().max(0.0) * 0.25).lerp(
53:         guard_rear_contact_separation(leg_length)?.metres(),
54:         longitudinal,
55:     ))
56: }
57: 
58: /// COM travel between centered open and closed contacts.
59: pub fn guard_contact_travel_distance(
60:     leg_length: SignedLength,
61:     local_direction: Vec2,
62: ) -> AnimationValueResult<NonnegativeLength> {
63:     NonnegativeLength::from_arithmetic(
64:         (guard_open_foot_separation(leg_length, local_direction)?.metres()
65:             - guard_closed_foot_separation(leg_length, local_direction)?.metres())
66:         .max(0.0)
67:             * 0.5,
68:     )
69: }
70: 
71: /// Maximum fore-aft guard stance immediately before the following foot lifts.
72: /// The ratio maps a 0.851688 m average-male thigh-plus-shank chain at 5'11" to
73: /// the requested one-yard stance, then scales directly with the actual rig.
74: pub fn guard_maximum_foot_separation(
75:     leg_length: SignedLength,
76: ) -> AnimationValueResult<NonnegativeLength> {
77:     NonnegativeLength::from_arithmetic(leg_length.metres().max(0.0) * 1.073_632_5)
78: }
79: 
80: /// Maximum fore-aft separation when the rear foot returns beside the front
81: /// foot. This maps the same 5'11" reference leg to the requested three inches.
82: pub fn guard_rear_contact_separation(
83:     leg_length: SignedLength,
84: ) -> AnimationValueResult<NonnegativeLength> {
85:     NonnegativeLength::from_arithmetic(leg_length.metres().max(0.0) * 0.089_469_37)
86: }

53: impl ProceduralAnimationConfig {
54:     pub(super) fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), TacticalCombatConfigError> {
55:         let response = self.body_response;
56:         if response.maximum_presentation_sample_gap_ticks == AnimationSampleSpan::ZERO

61:                 "invalid procedural animation tuning",

64:         Ok(())

40: pub struct RagdollMusclesConfig {
41:     /// Overall tone; zero is a fully passive corpse.

83: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
84: #[serde(try_from = "Option<f32>", into = "Option<f32>")]
85: pub enum MuscleRelease {
86:     Never,
87:     After(PositiveAnimationDuration),

90: impl TryFrom<Option<f32>> for MuscleRelease {
91:     type Error = AnimationValueError;
92:     fn try_from(seconds: Option<f32>) -> AnimationValueResult<Self> {
93:         match seconds {
94:             None => Ok(Self::Never),
95:             Some(seconds) => PositiveAnimationDuration::try_from(seconds).map(Self::After),
96:         }
97:     }
98: }
99: impl From<MuscleRelease> for Option<f32> {
100:     fn from(release: MuscleRelease) -> Self {
101:         match release {
102:             MuscleRelease::Never => None,
103:             MuscleRelease::After(age) => Some(age.seconds()),
104:         }
105:     }
